Subject: Redwood migration + OpenAI compatibility - post-call recap

Hey Alex / Emily —

Great to chat earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the technical POC: 

What we heard from FinCo:
- Primary goal: migrate inference from Hyperscaler X/OpenAI API to a Redwood-hosted or dedicated deployment while keeping SDK and prompt surface area minimal.
- Must preserve OpenAI-compatible API behavior for caller code (python SDK / REST).
- Success metrics: parity on prompt outputs for 90% of test prompts, latency below 150ms p95 for small-chat flows, and cost target ~40% of current per-token spend.
- Compliance ask: SOC2 + data residency in us-east region.

Redwood proposed POC scope:
1) OpenAI-compat smoke tests: run finite set (100) of representative prompts and compare outputs / token counts (prompt diffs).
2) SDK swap validation: run your python client tests against our OpenAI-compatible endpoints; confirm parameter mapping (model, temperature, max_tokens, top_p, stop).
3) Latency/cost baseline: run parallel load tests for 1-2 core flows to measure p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
4) Edge cases: streaming responses, function/tool-calls parity, and retry semantics.

Requested from FinCo before we start:
- A short sample prompt set (10–20 canonical prompts) and a couple of longer conversations for chat regression testing.
- Preferred test environment: hosted sandbox (fast onboarding) or Dedicated sandbox (closer to production).
- Any existing scripts/observability checks you run today to compute token counts and scoring.

Proposed timeline:
- You share sample prompts by Thu 3/12 -> We run initial smoke tests by Fri 3/13 -> Debrief early week of 3/16 with results and follow-ups.

Attachments: feel free to reply with sample prompts (or just paste a few here). We can also share a checklist and SDK migration guide if helpful — happy to loop in our SE to coordinate the technical plan.

Thanks,

Subject: POC test plan + OpenAI-compat checklist

Hi Alex / Marissa —

Thanks for the prompts, Alex. Quick tech plan and what we'll deliver for the smoke POC: 

1) Environment & creds
- We'll provision a hosted sandbox in us-east and share sandbox API keys (short-lived) by EOD Thu 3/12. Sandbox endpoints will be OpenAI-compatible: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions for parity.

2) Test matrix (initial):
- Models: rwd-gpt-3.5-equivalent, rwd-gpt-4-equivalent (mapping provided).
- Parameters: temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, streaming vs non-streaming, function/tool call payloads.
- Compare outputs by normalized edit distance and token count. We aim for >90% semantic parity on short prompts and manual review on longer flows.

3) SDK swap validation
- We'll provide a drop-in python snippet that mirrors your existing OpenAI calls (example below). Please run your unit tests against the sandbox key and share any mismatches.

Example python replace snippet:
# old: openai.ChatCompletion.create(... )
# new: import redwood
# response = redwood.ChatCompletion.create(model='rwd-gpt-3.5-equivalent', messages=messages, temperature=0.7)

4) Prompt diffs & tooling
- We'll generate a per-prompt diff report (text diffs + token delta) and surface any safety filter or tokenization differences.
- We'll also run a small streaming parity test (n=20) to compare chunking and event ordering.

5) Observability & logs
- We'll capture latency percentiles, token counts, and raw outputs. If you can share any scoring scripts you use today, we can run them locally to compute heuristic parity scores.

6) Deliverables & timeline
- Thu 3/12: sandbox API keys + attachments (compatibility checklist, SDK migration guide).
- Fri 3/13: smoke test results (diff report + latency/cost baseline).
- Early week of 3/16: debrief and next steps (dedicated run / throughput).

Attachments included: redwood-openai-compat-checklist.xlsx, redwood-sdk-migration-guide.pdf

A couple of implementation notes we've seen in past migrations:
- Tokenization differences usually explain small output deltas; we'll flag where behavior is semantic vs tokenizer-driven.
- Streaming chunk sizes can differ slightly by runtime; we preserve user-facing event ordering but chunk boundaries may vary.
- For function/tool calls, ensure schemas are identical; we'll emulate your call/response to confirm.

Alex — once you validate the sandbox key, run your smoke tests and paste any failing prompt IDs here. We'll prioritize fixes and follow with a dedicated run if throughput is a blocker.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
